None blocked. Kamo no Okusu, the other candidate this pass looked at, turned out to be a duplicate: it is already published as kag_010, The Great Camphor of Kamo, inside Kagoshima's own city file (same coordinates, same Aira shrine). Nothing new was needed there; it is simply removed from this leads list. 2026-09-03 write pass (session, following verify batches d1/d2/d3): 5 verified trees published as new single-tree places under the 2026-08-31 exception (Atami ata_001, Nagi ngi_001, Odawara oda_001, Ora ora_001, Ichinohe ich_001), each with strong documented fame evidence (national designation plus an annual festival, founding legend with DNA corroboration, or an active town tourism programme). leads.name: Senbon Icho / Senbon Koson-ju, Katsushika Hachimangu
leads.species_basis: confirmed by name and multiple sources (ja.wikipedia, Ichikawa city cultural-heritage page)
leads.note: CORRECTED COORDINATES, 2026-09-04 (famousjapan-batch1 verify pass). The original 'Senbon Icho' entry in this file carried coordinates 31.48857/130.742443, which land in Tarumizu, Kagoshima on an unrelated modern (planted from 1953) private ginkgo garden of ~1,200 trees, not this tree. The photographs attached to that entry (Katsushika-hachimangu filenames) actually belong to THIS shrine: Katsushika Hachimangu, 4-2-1 Yawata, Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture. This ginkgo is a real single-specimen candidate: goshinboku estimated over 1,200 years old, height 22m, root girth 10.2m, trunk girth 10.8m, named 'Senbon' (thousand-trunk) because many shoots rose from the base after lightning split the original trunk, National Natural Monument since 1931-02-20, white-snake legend attached. Sources: ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/葛飾八幡宮, city.ichikawa.lg.jp/culture/24242.html. Not verified to ship-ready in this pass (out of scope for a Kagoshima-focused batch, and outside this pass's four-candidate limit); worth a dedicated Ichikawa/Chiba pass, checking day-trip distance to Tokyo before deciding its container.

blocked.name: Miracle Pine Tree
blocked.reason: Checked 2026-09-03. The original pine died from saltwater intrusion after the 2011 tsunami's ground subsidence let seawater into its roots. What stands today at the Takata Matsubara Tsunami Recovery Memorial Park is a preserved monument built from much of the original wood plus a steel core and artificial replica parts, not a living tree. Never ships as an entry per the never-dead rule; may be mentioned as context inside a different living-tree story about the region.

blocked.name: Tsurugaoka Hachimangu ginkgo tree
blocked.reason: Checked 2026-09-03. The original roughly 1,000-year-old ginkgo trunk toppled in a storm on 10 March 2010 (confirmed by multiple Japanese news sources including Kanagawa Shimbun). The felled section was cut down and replanted 7m from the original spot, and new shoots (hikobae) sprouted from the surviving root a month later, so there may be a living regrowth from the same root system today, comparable to the Elm of Saint-Gervais precedent. Not delivered this pass because the current height/condition of that regrowth 16 years on was not established within the time box; a future pass could verify it as a living-succession entry rather than presenting the felled 1000-year trunk as still standing.

blocked.name: Tree of philosophy
blocked.reason: Checked 2026-09-03. This Biei, Hokkaido poplar was felled by its landowner on 24 February 2016 (multiple Japanese news sources, e.g. Nikkei and ITmedia), due to age-related collapse risk and damage tourists were causing to the surrounding farmland. Dead/gone, never ships per the never-dead rule.

blocked.name: Wilson's Stump
blocked.reason: Stump of a yakusugi felled roughly 500 years ago (named for E.H. Wilson who documented it in 1914); dead, not a living tree. Never ships as an entry per the never-dead rule. May be mentioned as context inside a living Yakushima tree story (its three living descendants growing nearby could be a separate future lead).

blocked.name: Natural habitat of Pyrus calleryana in Tado
blocked.reason: Official designation is "Tado Inunashi Natural Habitat" (多度のイヌナシ自生地), a ~0.3ha / 3,000sqm protected wild population of endangered Pyrus calleryana var. dimorphophylla on Mt Tado, Kuwana, Mie, designated National Natural Monument 2010-08-05. A habitat/population, not one identifiable tree or a compact ensemble with one place to stand. Rejected per brief instruction.

blocked.name: Okina sugi
blocked.reason: Fell on 10 September 2010 (confirmed by two independent Japanese news sources, Nikkei and a Yahoo News/local report): the trunk was roughly 90 percent hollow/decayed internally and could not bear the weight of its own upper 20m. Was the second-largest-girth Yakusugi (12.6m/1260cm) after Jomon Sugi, estimated age about 2,000 years, height 23.7m before falling, standing at about 1000m elevation on the Jomon Sugi trail. Now dead/fallen, so it never ships as an entry per the never-dead rule. The Commons photos in the lead file likely predate the 2010 fall and would misrepresent it as standing today.

blocked.name: Phoenix Trees Exposed to the A-bomb
blocked.reason: Confirmed mismatch, checked per brief instruction 2026-09-01. The Commons file File:Aogiri_Yokohama_Sakae.jpg carries its own caption and geotag: this is a second-generation aogiri (Firmiana simplex, Chinese Parasol Tree) planted at Earth Plaza (Chikyu Shimin Kanagawa Plaza) in Sakae-ku, YOKOHAMA, photographed 17 August 2025. It is a young sapling grown from the SEED of the trees that survived the Hiroshima bombing 1.3km from the hypocentre, not a tree itself exposed to the bomb, and it does not stand in Hiroshima at all. "Phoenix" in the lead name is the English nickname for aogiri (Chinese Parasol Tree), not the palm genus Phoenix; the leads file's own "Date Palm (Phoenix sp.)" species guess is a genus misread from that nickname and is wrong on every axis: wrong species, wrong history (second-generation descendant, not an original hibaku tree) and wrong location (Yokohama, not Hiroshima). Never chase this as a bombed original in Hiroshima. It COULD in principle become its own honestly-described lead someday (a peace-memorial aogiri sapling in Sakae-ku, Yokohama, correctly named and species-corrected), but that is a new, separate research question, not this entry, and the tree is very young rather than old.

blocked.name: Hiramatsu no utsukushimatsu jiseichi
blocked.reason: Checked per brief 2026-09-01. Official designation is Hiramatsu no Utsukushimatsu Jiseichi (平松のウツクシマツ自生地), a National Natural Monument (designated 3 March 1921) in KONAN CITY, SHIGA PREFECTURE (not Kyoto city, though within day-trip range at ~28km), protecting a wild population of Utsukushimatsu, a naturally radial-branching form of Japanese red pine (Pinus densiflora forma umbraculifera) that grows together on the southeast slope of Mt Bishozan. This is the only place this growth form occurs as a natural stand. Confirmed via Japanese Wikipedia and the Agency for Cultural Affairs database (online.bunka.go.jp), both found via search. A HABITAT/POPULATION covering a hillside, not one identifiable tree or a compact ensemble with one obvious place to stand; rejected on the same grounds as the Tado Inunashi habitat already blocked in this file. Also actively declining: multiple sources note rapid pine-wilt-disease losses in recent years despite local conservation efforts, which would make an alive-now claim for any single specimen within it hard to stand behind without visiting. A separate lead already in this file, "Nento-Hiramatsu Pine Tree" (Commons category Nento-Hiramatsu Park, no coordinate yet), may be an individually named specimen near or within this habitat and could be worth checking on its own in a future pass; not researched here, out of scope for this brief.

blocked.reason: Verified as real, alive and remarkable (Japan's largest known Sawara cypress, National Natural Monument 1974) but stands on private farmland managed for generations by the Usami family; no source establishes a public viewing point. Blocked under hard rule 10, 2026-09-02. A later pass could call Iwaki's tourism office to check for a public viewpoint.

blocked.name: Hagurosan no Sugi Namiki
blocked.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
blocked.reason: Not a single tree: this is the collective cedar avenue (Sugi Namiki) along the 1.8km stone sando up Mt Haguro, itself designated a special natural monument as a group of 500+ cedars 350-500 years old. All Commons photos show the avenue/path in snow, not one named specimen. The one individually famous tree among them, Jiji Sugi ('Grandpa Cedar', 1000+ years, the largest and oldest), is a distinct named tree and is delivered separately (see Hagurosan no Jiji Sugi, published as trk_001). This avenue entry fails the collectible-point rule (avenue/wood, CLAUDE.md La Rambla precedent). blocked.name: Higashi Akuragawa Inunashi Jiseichi
blocked.reason: Not a single tree: this is a national Natural Monument habitat site (jiseichi) protecting the wild population of Pyrus calleryana var. (Inu-Nashi), designated 1922 as the type locality where botanist Makino Tomitaro described the species. It is a scientific/botanical reserve covering a population of wild pear trees, not one named specimen; Commons photos are aerial habitat photographs and a 1921 government sketch of the habitat, not a tree portrait. Fails the collectible-point rule (habitat site, not a single tree). Source: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%9D%B1%E9%98%BF%E5%80%89%E5%B7%9D%E3%82%A4%E3%83%8C%E3%83%8A%E3%82%B7%E8%87%AA%E7%94%9F%E5%9C%B0

blocked.name: Kakunodate no Shidarezakura
blocked.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
blocked.reason: Not a single tree: this is the collective name for the National Natural Monument covering ~147-162 individually designated weeping cherries (Edo-higan cultivar) among roughly 400 total, planted on private samurai-house properties along ~2km of Bukeyashiki-dori. Japanese Wikipedia states outright it is a 'shorthand for about 150 trees' (約150本の総称である), designated as a group in 1974 (153 trees then, ~147 by 1999-2000 after storm losses); Semboku city's own tourism page confirms 162 of ~400 trees hold the designation today. All Commons photos are titled 'Bukeyashiki Street in Kakunodate', i.e. street views of the avenue, not a photo of one named specimen. No single stand-out individually-named tree distinct from the avenue was found in English or Japanese sources. Fails the project's collectible-point rule (CLAUDE.md, the Barcelona/La Rambla precedent): an avenue of ~150-400 trees along a 2km street has no single obvious place to stand. Sources checked: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%A7%92%E9%A4%A8%E3%81%AE%E3%82%B7%E3%83%80%E3%83%AC%E3%82%B6%E3%82%AF%E3%83%A9 and https://www.city.semboku.akita.jp/en/sightseeing/spot/07_shidare.html.

blocked.name: Great Muku of Futami
blocked.reason: Verified 2026-09-03 (National Natural Monument, Gojo City, girth 850cm, age given only as roughly 1,000 years across sources with no cited basis). Blocked, not held: Gojo City's own page states the tree stands 'in the garden of a private residence,' with only its canopy overhanging the municipal road. Hard rule 10's home test does not bend for canopy visibility, whatever the register or a city page says. Full record in data/research/famousjapan-batch-d2-verified.json (id goj_001).

blocked.name: Tsunekami no Sotetsu
blocked.reason: Verified 2026-09-04: alive, nationally designated (National Natural Monument, 9 Dec 1924), roughly 1300 years old, 8 trunks (5 tall 4.5-6.5m + 3 short 1.5-3.0m), base girth 520cm, but ja.wikipedia and prefecture/town sources agree it stands "in the yard of a private residence, in an alley between densely packed houses near the fishing port" in Tsunekami, Wakasa, Fukui. No source names any public viewing arrangement. Blocked under hard rule 10 (private land, not genuinely open to visitors), same class as Great Muku of Futami (goj_001) and Sawajiri no O Hinoki. Also note for any future look: it is a single Cycas revoluta specimen with 8 trunks from one base, so it is a collectible point in principle (not a grove/plant-community problem), the access problem alone blocks it.

blocked.name: Kiire no ryukyukogai sanchi (Kiire Kandelia obovata colony)
blocked.reason: Verified 2026-09-04: real and alive, Special National Natural Monument (designated 29 March 1952) at Kiire-Nomi, Kagoshima City, protecting the northernmost naturally-growing colony of Kandelia obovata (mehirugi), a mangrove species. Local tradition holds it was transplanted here from Ryukyu around 1609. This is explicitly a designated GROWTH SITE / colony ("産地", plant-community/habitat), not one identifiable tree: the designation and every source describe a stand of mangroves along a stream/tidal area, with no single specimen singled out. Blocked as an ensemble/habitat under the one-collectible-point rule (a grove or a whole wood is blocked, same as an avenue), not for any evidence or access reason. Could resurface later only as a place-level feature (e.g. "see the mangroves at Kiire") rather than as a tree entry, which is outside this pass's scope.

blocked.name: Ono no shidare-guri jiseichi
blocked.reason: Verified 2026-09-04 (famousjapan-batch3): a national Natural Monument (1920-07-17) covering a roughly 2.24 hectare natural-growth habitat of 800-900+ weeping/pendulous chestnut trees (a spontaneous mutant form, locally 'tengu no kuri'), one of about five known sites of this variant in Japan. This is a population/area designation, not one named specimen or a compact ensemble with one obvious place to stand, so it fails the single-collectible-point rule the same way an avenue or a whole wood does; the single-famous-tree exception is for one tree, not a forest population. No city currently published near this site (Tatsuno, Nagano Prefecture).

blocked.name: Nōin-hōshi Amagoi no Kusunoki (Nōin's Rain-Praying Camphor)
blocked.species: Camphor Tree (Camphora officinarum, syn. Cinnamomum camphora)

Not the same tree as the already-published omi_001 Ikiki no Gomon / The Living Gate (a separate, still-living camphor ~0.1km away at the same shrine). Verified 2026-09-04 famous-trees sweep.

blocked.name: Ibuki Yama Ibuki Juso
blocked.reason: Checked 2026-09-04 (famous-japan batch F1). National Natural Monument since Taisho 11 (1922), Ibaraki Prefectural Board of Education page (kyoiku.pref.ibaraki.jp) confirms: a grove of 8 Chinese juniper (Juniperus chinensis) trees on the north/south sides of a hill in Hitachi City, ~400 years old, not one tree with an obvious place to stand. Since 1996 the trees have been declining and being propagated/replaced; a Jan 2023 survey found only one surviving successor. Blocked as a grove/population designation, not a single collectible point. Sources: kyoiku.pref.ibaraki.jp/bunkazai/kuni-126/, Wayback snapshot of edu.pref.ibaraki.jp's original page, ffpri.go.jp r5_0123 report.

blocked.name: Uenohara no Okeyaki
blocked.reason: Checked 2026-09-04 (famous-japan batch F2). Real, alive National Natural Monument (designated 1944), zelkova, ~800-850 years old, 28m tall, 8.64m girth; ja.wikipedia.org and the city's own education-board page corroborate closely (coordinate would confirm to 35.629694/139.112861). Blocked under hard rule 10: the tree stands on the front grounds of Uenohara Elementary School, and the prefecture's own tourism page (yamanashi-kankou.jp) says visitors must contact school staff via intercom for approval first, the doorbell/reception-desk case the schools exception names as a no. No public-path or weekend-opening workaround found in either the city board's page or Wikipedia. Sources: ja.wikipedia.org's own page on the tree, yamanashi-kankou.jp/kankou/spot/p1_4072.html, city.uenohara.yamanashi.jp/site/kyoiku/1567.html.
